summary: The current causal graph is internally coherent for GEV and correctly links reliable electricity, grids, gas turbines, AI data-center demand and grid-equipment scarcity. However it is still a one-company world model; successor bottlenecks, cross-company dependency chains and substitution pathways are materially under-covered, so the structural lane cannot claim acquisition complete.

materialFindings.finding: The graph contains explicit sourced links from GEV to reliable electricity, power-grid infrastructure, gas turbines, AI-data-center demand and constrained grid-equipment capacity, with confidence values in the high-80s to high-90s and explicit structural signals/falsifiers.
materialFindings.decisionRelevance: This is a valid prototype for Evidence → Causal Effect → Factor reasoning rather than direct narrative-to-score jumps.

materialFindings.finding: The graph models grid-equipment capacity as a bottleneck but does not yet represent what becomes limiting if transformer/switchgear/gas-turbine capacity expands successfully—for example fuel infrastructure, interconnection/permitting, transmission construction, skilled labor, cooling/water, copper/electrical materials or generation-fuel constraints.
materialFindings.decisionRelevance: Predicting successor bottlenecks is essential to avoid over-owning today's constraint after the market/capacity response begins solving it.

materialFindings.finding: Only GEV is currently represented as a company node despite a 250-company active universe.
materialFindings.decisionRelevance: Earth cannot yet propagate shocks or identify second/third-order beneficiaries/fragilities across AI compute, power, cooling, materials, grid, nuclear, space, robotics and other dependencies.

materialFindings.finding: The existing GEV structural signals include explicit falsifiers tied to demand, order contraction, lead-time normalization, pricing contribution and margins.
materialFindings.decisionRelevance: This is strong causal hygiene and should be required for every new material structural signal rather than only for the first publishable company.

proposedCanonicalChanges.proposal: Build a sourced successor-bottleneck map around the current power/AI chain before promoting new structural edges: grid equipment → transmission/interconnection/permitting → generation/fuel → cooling/water → electrical materials/labor. Each node/edge should require a horizon, confidence and falsifier.
proposedCanonicalChanges.reason: This directly targets constraint migration and prevents static bottleneck assumptions.

proposedCanonicalChanges.proposal: As the next underwriting packages are created, add causal nodes/edges for RKLB, CRDO and ALAB only after primary evidence supports their role; do not infer structural importance from seed class.
proposedCanonicalChanges.reason: This grows the world model together with evidence rather than allowing an unsourced 250-node graph.

unknowns.detail: The system has not yet established which constraint becomes dominant after current grid/generation manufacturing expansions.

The current GEV graph does not yet encode enough competing generation, storage, demand-management or grid-architecture substitution paths to quantify how the causal thesis weakens under alternate technology trajectories.
No sufficiently broad company dependency graph exists yet to propagate geopolitical, commodity, regulatory or technology shocks through the full active universe.

peerRequests.request: Search for evidence that today's grid/generation bottlenecks are being solved faster than expected and identify emerging successor constraints not yet represented in Earth.

Attack the GEV structural thesis with substitution scenarios: faster storage, distributed generation, demand response, competing turbine/grid suppliers, permitting changes and any factor that could weaken scarcity rents.
For each new baseline candidate, surface the exact physical/technical dependency and monetization path needed to create sourced causal edges; avoid theme membership as proof.

blockingIssues.detail: The causal graph contains only one company node from a 250-company universe, so structural acquisition is materially incomplete.
